title: ₹300 Ka Pizza: Domino's Franchise Owner Ke Haath Mein Kitna Aata Hai?
description: No scraped reels this week, so this is reasoning. Franchise ownership is a top dream for our audience, and Indian men 18-34 order pizza and wonder whether a franchise is easy money. The 'where the ₹ goes' reveal worked for the Blinkit ₹518 order and the UPI explainer. Franchise terms and store-level numbers are public in annual reports.
text:
HISAAB FACT SHEET: QSR (Domino's pizza) store economics in India
Prepared 3 Nov 2026. Items marked [DERIVED] are my own arithmetic on a sourced number. Items marked [UNVERIFIED] come from low-quality sources.

**0. READ THIS FIRST: the franchise angle needs a reframe**

- Jubilant FoodWorks (JFL) is the master franchisee, not a franchisor selling stores to individuals. JFL and Domino's Pizza International Franchising signed a Master Franchise Agreement on 31 March 2026, renewing exclusive rights to develop and operate Domino's stores in India for 15 years. [https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/jubilant-foodworks-renews-dominos-franchise-for-15-years-126040101142_1.html]
- The renewal includes an option to extend for another 10 years. [https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/jubilant-foodworks-renews-15-year-dominos-master-franchise-for-india-sri-lanka-and-bangladesh]
- The financial terms of the renewal were not disclosed. [https://www.storyboard18.com/brand-marketing/jubilant-foodworks-secures-dominos-india-franchise-for-15-more-years-extends-regional-grip-93843.htm]
- Domino's stores in India are run by JFL itself, and a secondary source says JFL does not sell franchises to individuals and warns about fraud. [https://theguidex.com/dominos-franchise-in-india/] I did not find that warning on an official JFL page, so verify it before using it on screen.
- Another guide says individual franchise access is unlikely unless Jubilant FoodWorks confirms otherwise in writing. [https://wise.com/gb/blog/dominos-franchise-cost-in-india]
- Many "Domino's franchise cost" pages exist, but I found no official JFL source for their numbers. They contradict each other:
  - Total investment is quoted as ₹50–70 lakh [https://franchisemetric.com/dominos-franchise-cost-in-india/], ₹70 lakh to ₹2 crore or more [https://www.businessunfold.com/dominos-franchise-cost-in-india/], and ₹70 lakh to ₹3 crore [https://askdaman.com/dominos-franchise-cost-in-india/].
  - The franchise fee is quoted anywhere from ₹10–15 lakh [https://bosswallah.ai/blog/local-business/dominos-franchise-cost-india-2025-fees-investment/] to ₹30–50 lakh. [https://askdaman.com/dominos-franchise-cost-in-india/]
  - The "5.5% royalty + 4% ad fee" figure is repeated widely. It looks like the US franchise structure copied into Indian guides, because one Quora answer attributes it to a $25,000 franchise fee. [https://www.quora.com/What-is-the-cost-of-Dominos-pizza-franchise-to-own-in-India] Treat it as [UNVERIFIED] and don't show it as fact.
  - One site, jubilantfoodswork.com, claims to be an official franchise channel. The company's real documents sit on jubilantfoodworks.com, so the lookalike domain is a red flag. Do not use its numbers.
- Suggested reframe: "You can't buy a Domino's. The ₹300 pizza economics below are what JFL, the company that owns the stores, actually earns."

**1. What a store costs to set up**

- Official capex per store is not disclosed in the sources I found. The best figure is from a brokerage report (Centrum, March 2023): Domino's spends ₹11–12 million per store (₹1.1–1.2 crore), with ~₹30 million (₹3 crore) revenue per store per year and a payback of ~2 years. [https://centrumbroking.com/documents/Thematic_India_QSR_Sector_Centrum_20032023.pdf] This is an analyst estimate from 2023.
- The same report says other QSR chains have store paybacks of more than 3 years. [https://centrumbroking.com/documents/Thematic_India_QSR_Sector_Centrum_20032023.pdf]
- A blog puts setup at ₹1.3–1.5 crore. [UNVERIFIED] [https://businessbehindstocks.com/blog/jubilant-foodworks-dominos-india-qsr-franchise-unit-economics-analysis]
- JFL guided FY27 capex at ₹750–900 crore. [https://tradebrains.in/indian-markets/jubilant-foodworks-at-52-week-low-can-dominos-growth-and-popeyes-expansion-turn-things-around-12679366]
- Brokerage Motilal Oswal says JFL has eight commissaries that can handle around 5,000 stores, so the supply-chain spend is mostly done. [https://tradebrains.in/indian-markets/jubilant-foodworks-at-52-week-low-can-dominos-growth-and-popeyes-expansion-turn-things-around-12679366]

**2. Sales per store**

- Mature-store average daily sales (ADS) were ₹83,155 in Q2 FY26 [https://www.bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/8948b9cf-1dc7-4d2e-848d-3be0e20df5bd.pdf]. This is the official company figure. In Q1 FY26 it was ₹85,396. [https://www.jubilantfoodworks.com/Uploads/Files/1221foodfile-EarningsPresentationandPR.pdf]
- [DERIVED] ₹83,155 × 365 ≈ ₹3.0 crore a year per mature store. That matches the Centrum ₹3 crore figure. It works out to roughly ₹25 lakh a month (₹83,155 × 30).
- Ignore the "₹1.3 lakh+ daily sales" claim on one blog. It is double the official ADS. [https://businessbehindstocks.com/blog/jubilant-foodworks-dominos-india-qsr-franchise-unit-economics-analysis]
- Domino's India had 2,601 stores at the end of Q2 FY27 (30 Sep 2026). [https://upstox.com/news/market-news/stocks/jubilant-food-works-registers-nearly-12-growth-in-revenue-from-operations-for-q2-fy-27-check-all-updates/article-201474/]
- Q2 FY27 like-for-like (same-store) growth was 4.1%, up from 2.5% in Q1 FY27. [https://www.sahi.com/news/jubilant-foodworks-q2-fy27-consolidated-revenue-rises-11-9-to-2-608-7-crore] That is a big slowdown from 9.1% in Q2 FY26. [https://images.assettype.com/bloombergquint/2025-11-14/ok7n62sl
